messages:
Priya: Trying to onboard a MistralX->Gemma converted checkpoint (int4 test run). Generation looks fine for first 8 tokens then diverges weirdly (repeats, then softmax collapse). Anyone seen a head-packing or rotary packing issue crop up specifically with our int4 converter?

Sam: Yep. Two common culprits: (1) converter left qkv interleaved per-head instead of grouped by q/k/v, (2) rotary freq table stored with head-major ordering different from runtime. Both cause attention to degrade mid-sequence.

Jules: Quick sanity checks: compare shapes of qkv weight and rotary table. If qkv is (heads, 3, head_dim) vs (3, heads, head_dim) we need to reorder. Also check quantization layout (NHWC vs NCHW-style packing) because int4 packers sometimes bitpack across heads.

Priya: Dumped shapes: 
```
transformer.layers.0.attn.qkv.weight torch.Size([3072, 1024])
rotary.freqs torch.Size([32, 128])
```
Converter log: "packed_qkv=true" but no explicit reorder step.

Sam: That log flag is the clue. When packed_qkv is true the converter created qkv in [head,3,dim] pack. Runtime expects [3,head,dim]. You can do a lazy fix in the loader: reshape to (heads,3,head_dim) -> permute(1,0,2) -> reshape back.

Jules: For int4 we also saw a subtle bug: the packing step was using a different endianness for nibbles on one build of faisspack. If you run the same binary on two hosts with different lib versions, you can get different dequantized values. Check ldd on the quant lib.

Priya: Interesting — on host A (dev) outputs were fine; on host B (ci) we saw divergence. ldd shows faisspack v1.2 on A and v1.1 on B.

Sam: Bingo. Faisspack 1.1 had a nibble-order bug that was fixed in 1.2. The converter pipeline used the newer packer locally but ci used the older runtime library. That would create reproducible but wrong dequant values.

Priya: After swapping packer lib on CI to v1.2, the int4 outputs aligned longer but still diverged at token ~20. I then applied a qkv reorder (in loader) and that fixed the remaining mismatch. Now matches reference for 256 tokens.

Jules: Nice. Can you paste the reorder snippet you used? I'll add it to our onboarding toolkit.

Priya: Snippet: 
```
# loader patch
w = state['transformer.layers.0.attn.qkv.weight']
# expected (3, heads, head_dim, in_dim)
h = num_heads
hd = w.shape[0] // (3*h)
w = w.view(h, 3, hd, -1).permute(1,0,2,3).contiguous().view(3*h*hd, -1)
state['transformer.layers.0.attn.qkv.weight'] = w
```
Worked for us.

Sam: On docs: also add a tokenizer checksum step. We found a case where special sentinel tokens had different ids across tokenizer builds which shifts cache alignment and manifests as early divergence. A one-line test: tokenizer.encode("\u2581") should match across envs.

Priya: Added to followups: onboard-494 (converter flag --emit-packed-layout), onboard-495 (loader auto-reorder fallback), infra-quant-33 (pin faisspack >=1.2 in CI), docs-rotary-quickcheck.

ops-bot: CI: created issue onboard-495 (auto-reorder fallback) from thread by Priya.

Jules: For completeness, we should run our eval harness (seeded generation + ppl checks + exact-token check) before marking conversion done. I'll add a unit that checks first 64 tokens equal to oracle when seed fixed.

Priya: Will open PR with converter flag and loader fallback. Thanks for the quick triage team :rocket:

Sam: Thanks. Saved us from a sneaky quant+layout combo.
